## About this dataset

In the Florida Everglades, fire is a key driver of ecological dynamics, interacting with hydrology and vegetation structure. Fires have been recorded by Everglades National Park and Big Cypress National Preserve (1978-2023) by mapping the outer boundary of fires. Annual fire perimeter data for the two regions were combined to generate a fire history database for the subtropical landscape. This dataset includes fire perimeters, binary burned layers, and years of fire layers that can be used to quantify fire dynamics across subtropical ecosystems.

## Variables

_See the data package metadata for the full list of variables, units and uncertainty._

_Units, definitions and uncertainty are documented in the archived metadata (EML)._

## Research applications

- Fire frequency and time-since-fire analyses
- Linking fire regimes to hydrology and vegetation change

## Known limitations

- Perimeters are outer boundaries; unburned islands inside fires are not mapped

## Get the data with code

::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# install.packages("EDIutils")
library(EDIutils)

pkg <- "edi.1953.1"
entities <- read_data_entity_names(pkg)   # list the files in the package
entities

# read the first entity into R
raw <- read_data_entity(pkg, entities$entityId[1])
dat <- readr::read_csv(raw)
```

### Python

```python
import io, requests, pandas as pd

pkg = "edi/1953/1"
base = "https://pasta.lternet.edu/package"
ids = requests.get(f"{base}/data/eml/{pkg}").text.split()
names = requests.get(f"{base}/name/eml/{pkg}").text
print(names)

csv = requests.get(ids[0]).content
df = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(csv))
```
